examples.en: I won't be attending this gathering.
Many people were absent from yesterday's meeting.
I skipped the event because I wasn't feeling well.

examples.ko: 친구는 일 때문에 결혼식에 불참할 거예요.
examples.en: My friend will miss the wedding because of work.
If you can't attend class, please let us know in advance.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 부상 때문에 경기에 불참하고 집에서 쉬어요.
examples.en: That player is sitting out the match because of an injury and resting at home.

explain: '참석하다'의 반대이고, 회의·행사·모임처럼 정해진 자리에 안 간다는 공식적인 느낌이 있어요. 가벼운 말로는 '안 가요', '못 가요'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of 참석하다 and sounds formal, used for meetings, events and gatherings. In casual speech people more often say 안 가요 or 못 가요.

examples.ko: 잘못하고도 사과를 안 하다니 정말 뻔뻔스러워요.
examples.en: It's really shameless not to apologize even after doing wrong.

examples.ko: 뻔뻔스러운 얼굴로 또 돈을 빌려 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: With a brazen face, he asked to borrow money again.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 거짓말을 하고도 뻔뻔스럽게 웃었어요.
examples.en: That person lied and still smiled shamelessly.

examples.ko: 약속을 어기고 뻔뻔스러웠던 그 친구가 미워요.
examples.en: I dislike that friend who broke the promise and had no shame about it.
He was so shameless that I was speechless.

examples.ko: 뻔뻔스럽지 않으면 그런 말은 못 해요.
examples.en: You can't say something like that unless you have no shame.

explain: '뻔뻔하다'와 뜻이 거의 같아요. 잘못을 하고도 부끄러워하지 않는 태도를 비난하는 말이라서 윗사람에게 직접 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Nearly the same as 뻔뻔하다. It criticizes someone who feels no shame after doing wrong, so you would not say it to someone older to their face.

examples.en: The new student is being left out in class.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때 친구들에게 소외당한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I was once shut out by my friends.

examples.ko: 회사에서 소외당하면 일할 맛이 안 나요.
examples.en: If you're left out at work, you lose the will to work.
He felt that his family had pushed him aside.

examples.ko: 나이 든 분들이 새 기술에서 소외당하지 않았으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope older people aren't left behind by new technology.
I was left out of the group and sat by myself.

explain: 다른 사람들이 나를 끼워 주지 않는다는 뜻이라서 당하는 쪽이 주어예요. 하는 쪽을 말할 때는 '소외시키다'를 써요. 학교·회사·사회 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The subject is the person being left out, by other people. The one doing it is described with 소외시키다. It often comes up when talking about school, work and society.

examples.en: I'm upset because my friends leave only me out.
Please don't deliberately leave anyone out.

examples.ko: 그 팀장은 새 직원을 소외시킨 적이 없어요.
examples.en: That team leader has never shut out a new employee.

examples.ko: 약한 사람을 소외시키는 사회는 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: A society that pushes weak people aside is not a good one.
The kids played while shutting one friend out.
They will push out the people who object.

explain: '소외당하다'와 짝이에요. 끼워 주지 않는 쪽이 주어일 때 이 말을 쓰고, 당하는 쪽이 주어일 때는 '소외당하다'를 써요. '따돌리다'는 더 일상적이고 직접적인 말이에요.
explain_en: This is the partner of 소외당하다. Use it when the subject is the one leaving others out; use 소외당하다 when the subject is the one left out. 따돌리다 is more everyday and more direct.

examples.en: Many villages were plundered during the war.
The shop was looted, so there's nothing left.
There was an incident where the museum's treasures were looted.
They say this cultural property was taken by force long ago.
The villagers stood guard so that nothing would be plundered.
The house was looted and burned down.

explain: '도둑맞다'는 몰래 훔쳐 간 경우이고, '약탈당하다'는 힘이나 폭력으로 빼앗긴 경우예요. 전쟁이나 역사 이야기에서 많이 써요. 하는 쪽을 말하면 '약탈하다'예요.
explain_en: 도둑맞다 is for things stolen secretly; 약탈당하다 is for things taken by force or violence, mostly in talk of war and history. The side doing it is 약탈하다.

examples.en: In the old days, soldiers plundered villages.
The thieves looted the store and ran away.
Plundering cultural property is a serious wrong.

examples.ko: 해적들이 배를 습격해서 물건을 약탈했다고 해요.
examples.en: They say pirates attacked ships and plundered the goods.

examples.ko: 사람들이 약탈할 수 없게 문을 단단히 잠갔어요.
examples.en: We locked the doors tight so people couldn't loot the place.
Things that were looted must be returned later.

explain: '훔치다'는 몰래 가져가는 것이고, '약탈하다'는 힘으로 여럿이 크게 빼앗는 것이에요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스와 역사 이야기에서 써요.
explain_en: 훔치다 is taking something secretly; 약탈하다 is taking things by force, often on a large scale. You meet it in news and history rather than everyday chat.

examples.en: The news said the police had taken the suspect in.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 연행 소식에 모두 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Everyone was surprised by the news of his being taken in.

examples.ko: 연행 과정에서 문제는 없었는지 확인하고 있어요.
examples.en: They are checking whether there were any problems during the arrest.
Detentions continued at the protest site.
Right after he was taken in, his family was contacted.
They explained the reason for the detention in front of the police station.

explain: 경찰이 사람을 조사하려고 경찰서로 데려가는 일이에요. '체포'는 법적으로 붙잡는 것이고 '연행'은 데려가는 것이라서, 뉴스에서는 두 말이 함께 나오기도 해요.
explain_en: This is when police take a person to the station for questioning. 체포 is the legal act of arresting; 연행 is the act of taking someone along, so news often uses both.

examples.en: The police take that man in.
The police took the thief in at the scene.
After taking the suspect in, they began questioning.

examples.ko: 경찰이 두 사람을 연행하고 차에 태웠어요.
examples.en: The police took two people in and put them in the car.

examples.ko: 증거가 없으면 함부로 연행할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Without evidence, they can't just take someone in.
When the police tried to take him in, he ran away.

explain: 주어는 거의 경찰이에요. '체포하다'는 법적으로 잡는 것이고 '연행하다'는 경찰서로 데려가는 것이에요. 일상에서는 '잡아가다'라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: The subject is almost always the police. 체포하다 is the legal arrest; 연행하다 is bringing someone to the station. In daily speech people also say 잡아가다.

en: have the upper hand; be superior; be dominant

examples.en: Our team has the upper hand in the game.

examples.ko: 지금은 파란 팀이 더 우세한 것 같아요.
examples.en: Right now the blue team seems to be ahead.
I had the edge in stamina.
We were ahead at first but lost at the end.
They say that candidate leads in the polls.
If the weather is clear, we'll have the advantage.

explain: '강하다'처럼 힘 자체를 말하기보다 상대와 비교해서 앞서 있다는 뜻이에요. 반대말은 '열세이다'이고, 스포츠와 선거 뉴스에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Rather than describing raw strength like 강하다, it means being ahead in comparison with an opponent. The opposite is 열세이다, and it appears often in sports and election news.

examples.en: That company is a leading firm in its industry.
I got into one of the top universities.
This city has many well-known hospitals.
He is one of the country's leading musicians.
Leading companies are taking part in this event.
I want to visit some of the world's best-known libraries.

explain: 주로 '유수한'으로 명사 앞에서 쓰고, '유수해요'처럼 끝맺는 일은 드물어요. 기업·대학·병원처럼 손꼽히는 곳을 말할 때 써요. 말할 때는 '유명한'이나 '손꼽히는'이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is used almost only as 유수한 before a noun; ending a sentence with 유수해요 is rare. It describes places that rank among the best, such as companies, universities and hospitals. In speech, 유명한 or 손꼽히는 sounds more natural.

examples.en: Thanks to the new system, costs go down.
The electricity bill went down a lot.

examples.ko: 시간이 절감되면 다른 일도 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If time is saved, we can do other things too.

examples.ko: 인건비가 절감된 만큼 서비스를 좋게 만들었어요.
examples.en: We improved the service by as much as labor costs were cut.
Material costs are down and the quality is the same.
I expect the costs to come down.

explain: 비용·시간·에너지처럼 줄이고 싶은 것이 줄어들 때 써요. 일부러 줄이는 쪽은 '절감하다', 그 결과로 줄어든 쪽은 '절감되다'예요. 사람이 느끼는 감정에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Used when costs, time or energy that you want to reduce actually go down. 절감하다 is cutting on purpose; 절감되다 is the result of being cut. It is not used for feelings.

examples.en: The company is cutting costs this year.

examples.ko: 불을 끄면 전기를 절감할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you turn off the lights, you can save electricity.
We made an app to save time.
We reduced waste by cutting down on packaging.
I'm looking for ways to cut expenses.

examples.ko: 예산을 절감하고 남은 돈으로 선물을 샀어요.
examples.en: We cut the budget and bought gifts with the leftover money.

explain: '줄이다'와 비슷하지만 비용·시간·에너지를 아낀다는 느낌이 강하고 회사나 뉴스에서 많이 써요. 같은 소리의 '절감하다'(마음 깊이 느끼다)는 다른 말이니 문맥으로 구분해요.
explain_en: Similar to 줄이다 but with a stronger sense of saving cost, time or energy, and common in business and news. There is another 절감하다 that means to feel something deeply, so tell them apart by context.

examples.en: My friend is arranging this song in a new way.
I rearranged an old song and sang it.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 직접 노래를 편곡하기도 해요.
examples.en: That singer sometimes arranges the songs herself.
The version arranged for piano is better.

examples.ko: 학교 축제 때 쓸 노래를 편곡할 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to arrange a song for the school festival.
We arranged it to suit the band and started practicing.

explain: 있는 곡의 멜로디는 두고 악기나 분위기를 바꾸는 일이에요. 새 곡을 처음 만드는 '작곡하다'와 달라요. 가수 소개나 음악 방송에서 '편곡'이라는 말이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: This means keeping a song's melody but changing the instruments or mood. It differs from 작곡하다, which is writing a new song. The noun 편곡 often appears in music credits and TV shows.

examples.ko: 현행 규칙으로는 이 일을 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Under the current rules, we can't do this.
Many people say we should change the current system.
According to the current law, this is illegal.

examples.ko: 현행 방식은 시간이 너무 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: The present method takes too long.
The current rates stay the same until next month.
The school explained the existing regulations to the students.

explain: '지금 쓰이고 있는'이라는 뜻으로 법·제도·규칙·요금 앞에 붙여 써요. '현재'는 시간 전반에 쓰지만 '현행'은 이렇게 제도 앞에 쓰는 말이에요. 사람이나 날씨에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It goes before words like law, system, rule or fee to mean 'the one in use now'. 현재 can describe time in general, but 현행 is used for systems and rules. It is not used for people or weather.

examples.en: He's sly, so it's hard to trust him.
Don't be fooled by deceitful words.
They say people's hearts are fickle indeed.
His attitude turned slippery once he got money.
I dislike the way he smiles so slyly.

examples.ko: 저는 간사하지 않은 사람과 친구가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be friends with someone who isn't deceitful.

explain: 자기에게 이득이 되면 태도를 쉽게 바꾸고 아첨하는 사람에게 쓰는 부정적인 말이에요. '마음이 간사하다'는 나도 모르게 편한 쪽으로 바뀐다는 뜻으로 자신에게도 써요.
explain_en: A negative word for someone who changes attitude easily when it benefits them and flatters people. 마음이 간사하다 is also said about oneself, meaning your heart drifts to the easier side.

examples.en: A pop-up performance was held downtown yesterday.
A sudden downpour poured down.
The shop announced a surprise sale.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 게릴라 콘서트로 팬을 놀라게 했어요.
examples.en: The singer surprised fans with an unannounced concert.

examples.ko: 게릴라 이벤트는 장소를 미리 알려 주지 않아요.
examples.en: Pop-up events don't tell you the place in advance.

examples.ko: 영화 속 게릴라 부대가 산으로 도망쳤어요.
examples.en: The guerrilla unit in the movie fled to the mountains.

explain: 원래 군사 쪽 말인데, 한국어에서는 '게릴라 콘서트', '게릴라 세일', '게릴라성 폭우'처럼 예고 없이 갑자기 하는 일 앞에 붙여 많이 써요.
explain_en: Originally a military term for irregular fighters, but in Korean it is mostly attached to sudden, unannounced things, as in 게릴라 콘서트, 게릴라 세일 and 게릴라성 폭우.

examples.en: The hunter aims at the bird.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 젊은 사람들을 겨냥한 제품을 냈어요.
examples.en: That company released a product aimed at young people.
I aimed carefully and threw the ball.
This ad was made with students in mind.

examples.ko: 그 말은 저를 겨냥한 것 같아서 기분이 안 좋았어요.
examples.en: That remark seemed aimed at me, so I felt bad.

examples.ko: 여름 방학을 겨냥하여 새 상품을 준비해요.
examples.en: We're preparing a new product with summer vacation in mind.

explain: '겨누다'처럼 총이나 공을 목표에 맞추는 뜻에서 출발했고, 지금은 '젊은 층을 겨냥한 상품'처럼 특정 대상이나 시기를 노린다는 뜻으로 더 자주 써요. '노리다'보다 중립적이에요.
explain_en: It started from pointing a gun or ball at a target like 겨누다, but today it is used more for aiming at a particular group or season, as in 젊은 층을 겨냥한 상품. It is more neutral than 노리다.

examples.en: I cut the apple with a knife and looked at the cross section.
You can see growth rings on the cross section of the tree.
The cut face of the cake looks really pretty.

examples.ko: 이 사건은 사회의 한 단면을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This incident shows one side of society.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 현대인의 생활 단면을 그렸어요.
examples.en: That movie portrayed a slice of modern people's lives.

examples.ko: 단면을 보면 안이 어떻게 생겼는지 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: Looking at the cross section, you can see what the inside is like.

explain: 물건을 잘랐을 때 보이는 자른 면이에요. 비유로 '사회의 한 단면'처럼 전체 중 한 부분을 보여 준다는 뜻으로도 많이 써요. 이때는 '모습'이나 '일부분'과 비슷해요.
explain_en: It is the cut face you see when you slice something. Figuratively, 사회의 한 단면 means one part that reveals the whole, close to 모습 or 일부분.

examples.en: That team is really formidable.

examples.ko: 막강한 힘을 가진 회사가 시장을 이끌어요.
examples.en: A powerful company leads the market.
The opposing player was too strong.

examples.ko: 막강한 군대를 가진 나라는 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Not many countries have a mighty army.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 캐릭터가 막강해서 이기기 쉬워요.
examples.en: In this game the character is so strong that winning is easy.
His influence is known to be enormous.

explain: '강하다'보다 훨씬 세서 맞서기 어렵다는 느낌이에요. 힘·권력·팀·군대·영향력처럼 규모가 큰 대상에 어울려요. 작은 물건이 단단하다고 할 때는 '튼튼하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Much stronger than 강하다, with a sense that it is hard to stand against. It fits big things such as power, authority, teams, armies and influence. For a small sturdy object, use 튼튼하다 instead.

en: all-around ability; being able to do everything

examples.en: My friend is great at both studying and sports.

examples.ko: 이 칼은 만능 도구라서 어디에나 써요.
examples.en: This knife is an all-purpose tool, so I use it everywhere.
I think money is not everything.
I want to become an all-around entertainer.

examples.ko: 만능 키가 있으면 모든 문을 열 수 있어요.
examples.en: With a master key, you can open every door.
The internet may look all-powerful, but it has limits.

explain: 무엇이든 다 잘하거나 다 해결된다는 뜻이에요. '만능 키', '만능 엔터테이너'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 많이 붙고, '돈이 만능은 아니다'처럼 부정으로도 써요.
explain_en: It means being good at, or solving, everything. It often sits before another noun, as in 만능 키 or 만능 엔터테이너, and is also used in the negative, as in 돈이 만능은 아니다.

examples.en: The doctor picked up the scalpel and began the surgery.
A scalpel is very sharp, so you have to be careful.
The scalpels are laid out cleanly in the operating room.
The nurse handed the doctor a scalpel.
The students dissected a frog with a scalpel.
With just one scalpel, he finished a hard operation.

explain: 수술할 때 쓰는 작은 칼이에요. 일상에서는 '수술용 칼'이라고도 해요. '메스를 가하다'는 문제를 고치려고 과감하게 손댄다는 비유로도 쓰여요.

phrases.en: We have to take a scalpel to the outdated system.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제를 고치려고 과감하게 손댄다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Figurative: to take bold action to fix a problem.

explain_en: A small knife used in surgery, also called 수술용 칼. The phrase 메스를 가하다 is used figuratively for taking bold action to fix a problem.

examples.en: He works as an aide to the president.
Assisting the president is very busy work.
I took on the role of assistant to the team leader.

examples.ko: 의원 보좌 일을 하면서 정치를 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned about politics while working as an aide to a lawmaker.

examples.ko: 좋은 보좌가 있으면 일이 훨씬 쉬워져요.
examples.en: With a good aide, work becomes much easier.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 오랫동안 시장의 보좌를 했어요.
examples.en: He served as the mayor's aide for a long time.

explain: 윗사람이나 중요한 사람 곁에서 일을 돕는 것이에요. 그냥 '도움'이나 '돕기'와 달리 높은 자리를 돕는다는 느낌이 있어요. 회사에서는 '비서'나 '보조'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: Helping a superior or an important person from close by. Unlike plain 도움, it implies assisting someone in a high position. In companies 비서 or 보조 is more common.

examples.en: I assist the team leader.
The secretary assisted the president from his side.
Ten staff members assist the mayor.

examples.ko: 새 총리를 보좌하고 일을 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm assisting the new prime minister and learning the job.
I came to work early to assist the mayor.
We're hiring someone to assist the CEO.

explain: 윗사람이 일을 잘하도록 곁에서 돕는다는 뜻이라서 도움을 받는 사람이 나보다 높은 자리예요. 친구를 돕는 일에는 '도와주다'를 쓰고, 이 말은 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It means helping a superior do their job well from close by, so the person helped holds a higher position. For helping a friend, use 도와주다 instead.

examples.en: The school doesn't allow cell phone use.
The city denied permission for the building work.
I don't know why the company refused the vacation.
The court will turn down that application.
The concert hall does not permit filming.

examples.ko: 사진 촬영을 불허하면 안내문을 붙여야 해요.
examples.en: If you don't allow photography, you have to post a notice.

explain: '허락하다'의 반대로 규칙이나 기관이 공식적으로 안 된다고 정하는 느낌이에요. 친구나 가족 사이에서는 '안 돼요', '못 하게 해요'라고 말해요. 공지·뉴스에서 자주 봐요.
explain_en: The opposite of 허락하다, with the feeling that a rule or institution officially says no. Among friends and family people say 안 돼요 or 못 하게 해요 instead. You see it often in notices and news.

en: personal expense; one's own money (out of pocket)

examples.ko: 선생님이 사비로 학생들에게 책을 사 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher bought books for the students with her own money.
I paid for the business trip out of my own pocket.
I spent my own money to hold the event.

examples.ko: 사비로 산 물건은 회사에서 돌려받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get back from the company what you bought with your own money.
He had a hard time because he used so much of his own money.

examples.ko: 감독님이 사비로 선수들에게 밥을 사 줬어요.
examples.en: The coach treated the players to meals out of his own pocket.

explain: 회사나 단체의 돈이 아니라 내 돈으로 낸다는 뜻이에요. 반대로 회사 돈은 '공금', 회사가 내 주는 비용은 '경비'라고 해요. '사비를 털다'처럼 아낌없이 쓴다는 표현도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means paying with your own money rather than a company's or group's. The opposite is 공금 (company funds), and costs the company covers are 경비. You'll also hear 사비를 털다 for spending freely out of pocket.
